name: Rione Monti
tagline: The postcard heart of the trulli
description: The largest and most famous trulli district, a dense hillside of over a thousand conical-roofed houses lining steep cobbled lanes. It is the town's main draw and busiest quarter, packed with day-trippers by day and quietly magical once they leave in the evening.
bestFor: First-time visitors who want to sleep among the trulli
cons: Very crowded at peak day-tripper hours
Steep cobbled lanes and tourist prices

name: Aia Piccola
description: The smaller, more residential trulli district across from Rione Monti, where locals still live and tourism feels gentler. Its narrow lanes are calmer and more authentic, offering the same conical-roofed beauty with far less commercial bustle and a genuine sense of everyday Alberobello life.
bestFor: Slow-travel nomads wanting a calm, local base
pros: Quieter and more authentic than Rione Monti
Still within the historic trulli core
Short walk to the town center

name: Piazza del Popolo and modern center
tagline: Everyday Alberobello away from the crowds
description: The modern town around Piazza del Popolo is where local life happens, with everyday shops, cafes, the train station, and services. It lacks the trulli fairy-tale looks but offers practicality, better value, and a normal rhythm just minutes from the historic districts.
bestFor: Longer stays prioritizing convenience and value
pros: Better value than the trulli core
Close to the train station and buses

name: Locorotondo
tagline: Whitewashed hilltop neighbor in the Valle d'Itria
description: A short trip away, Locorotondo is one of Italy's prettiest villages, a circular whitewashed hill town with flower-lined lanes and sweeping Valle d'Itria views. It makes a serene alternative base or an easy day trip, known for its crisp local white wine and unhurried charm.
bestFor: Nomads wanting quiet beauty and wine country
pros: Calmer and less touristy than Alberobello
